paragraphs: On Saturday at noon, the phone rang in the hall. Tom picked it up and said, "Hello, this is Tom." "Hi, Tom, this is Aunt Sue," said the person on the phone. Lily came to listen, because Aunt Sue was visiting the family that day. Her plane from the north was arriving at three o'clock. Dad was going to drive to the airport and meet her.

"I am at the airport now, but my plane is late," said Aunt Sue. "How late?" asked Tom. "It is arriving at half past four, not at three o'clock." Tom listened carefully. He wrote the new time on a piece of paper. "Would you tell Dad immediately?" asked Aunt Sue. "If he leaves at two o'clock, he will wait at the airport for a long time." "There are daily planes from the north," she added. "But this plane is the last one today."

Lily ran to the garden, and Tom stayed on the phone. Dad was in the garden. He stood next to the plants with a small bucket of water. "Dad, Aunt Sue's plane is late!" said Lily. "It is arriving at half past four." "Thank you, Lily," said Dad. "The drive to the airport takes forty minutes, so I will leave at half past three." Lily went back to the hall and told Tom the plan. Tom told Aunt Sue, and she said, "Good. If the plane is later again, I will call you."

"I have a surprise for Dad," said Aunt Sue. "In the airport shop, I found a striped tie." "It had a big discount." "Dad has only one tie, and it is gray," said Tom. "Now he will have two," said Aunt Sue, and she laughed. "Don't tell him about it, please." "We won't," said Tom, and he smiled at Lily.

At half past three, Dad took the car keys and left for the airport. Tom and Lily waited in the hall with Pip. At six o'clock, the car came back, and Aunt Sue got out with her luggage. Pip barked and ran in a circle around her. Aunt Sue laughed and gave him a pat. After dinner, Aunt Sue gave Dad a small box. Dad opened it and held up the striped tie. "This is a lovely surprise," he said. Everybody laughed, and Pip barked again.
